meta.title: "Do it this way or not at all" — but what else? Why there's almost always a third option | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to ask "what else?" and see the third option that was hidden from them. Game-based critical thinking course for children aged 10–16.

hero.headline: Does your child pick between two options — because no one showed them the others?
hero.subheadline: "Either you come with us, or you sit alone." "Do it this way or not at all." The options sound logical — and your child picks one. They don't even think there's a third, because no one named it.

media.alt: A child shown only two options, when there's a third

pain.title: It's not the limit of reality — it's a limit drawn for them
pain.body:
The child isn't shown all the options — only the ones that suit whoever is offering them. Two points sound like the full list, when in fact there's a third and a fourth right beside them. They just weren't mentioned.

This isn't "not looking" or being too lazy to think. The child simply wasn't shown the other possibilities — and the "either-or" frame looks complete in itself. Without the skill to notice it, they accept the offered options as the only ones possible and never ask whether there's anything beyond them.

The result — the child doesn't see the solutions that actually fit them. They pick from someone else's short list, thinking it's all of reality — and walk right past the option that would have been better for them.

social_proof.quote: My daughter used to see only "either-or" and pick one of the two. Now she asks "what other option is there?" — and often finds one nobody even mentioned.
social_proof.author: Olena, mum of 11-year-old Alice

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 10–16 year olds. At this age, children are receptive to new thinking patterns and are still forming their views.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.
